subtext: Built, rebuilt and tested by engineers who work on Land Rover engines every day.
Here's our practical view of the Rover K-Series across its Land Rover applications.

columns.title: APPLICATIONS WE SEE:
columns.body: The K-Series is the petrol option in the Freelander 1 — one of the most recognisable applications we work on from this era of Land Rover.

columns.title: WHAT WE REPLACE:
columns.body: Head gasket, cooling system components, timing belt, main bearings, connecting rod bearings, and complete gasket and seal set as standard on every rebuild, with cooling system components receiving particular attention.

columns.title: KNOWN ISSUES:
columns.body: The K-Series is notoriously prone to head gasket failure; it will blow, and more than once. Head gasket failure is driven by cooling system faults and overheating. Small coolant leaks can lead to overheating and head gasket failure. Dropped cylinder liners can require a new engine. The 1.8 K-Series petrol engine has an inherent design fault.

typical.title: LAND ROVER Rover K-Series REBUILD
typical.intro: The following describes a typical rebuild scope for this engine — illustrative of the work involved, not a specific customer job. Real case studies from our own completed work will replace this section once available.
typical.body: The K-Series is notoriously prone to head gasket failure — it will blow, and more than once. Head gasket failure is driven by cooling system faults and overheating, which is why we inspect the cooling system thoroughly on every rebuild. Small coolant leaks can lead to overheating and head gasket failure. Engines don't just blow head gaskets; they drop liners, requiring a new engine. Cooling system maintenance is critical — we replace the thermostat, water pump and hoses as part of a full rebuild.

scope.label: Typical Scope:
scope.text: Head gasket, cooling system components (thermostat, water pump, hoses), timing belt, bearings, gaskets
